items.answer: Landing page — 5–10 days. Corporate site — 2–3 weeks. Online store with integrations — from 4 weeks. Exact deadlines go into the contract after the brief.

items.question: We already have a site and a CRM, but they don't talk. Is that your job?
items.answer: Yes, that's our core work. We don't rebuild everything from scratch — we connect what already runs: site, CRM, accounting, marketplaces, telephony, shipping.

items.question: Why more expensive than a freelancer?
items.answer: Because the price includes a contract, a 12-month warranty, configured analytics and support. The warranty means we fix defects in the delivered code free of charge for 12 months, while new features are built by separate agreement. A freelancer is cheaper right up until they disappear — then you pay twice for the same thing.

items.question: What does post-launch support include?
items.answer: First month — free fixes and consulting. After that, by agreement. We don't disappear once we're paid.

items.question: Do you hand over access?
items.answer: Yes, all of it, immediately. Site, domain, hosting, analytics — they're yours. We don't hold clients hostage.

items.question: Do you work with existing sites?
items.answer: Yes, we do. We take a site in any condition — extend it, fix it, integrate it with everything else. And we build first sites from scratch just as often.

items.question: How does payment work?
items.answer: 50% upfront, 50% on delivery. For larger projects — in stages, with each stage's deliverable fixed in the contract. The next payment only comes after you've accepted the previous stage. We don't ask for money for the next step until the current one is closed.

items.question: What if I need something non-standard?
items.answer: Message us on Telegram and we'll talk it through. We've built integrations with Vapi, Binotel, SalesDrive, KeyCRM, Checkbox and Nova Poshta. Chances are we've done it already.

items.question: I've never sold online before. Where do I start?
items.answer: With a conversation about the product and the buyer, not with a website. On the free assessment we work out what you sell, who to and what sets you apart — and only then say which type of site you need and what it costs. If the idea doesn't hold up to the numbers, we'll tell you straight rather than take your money for a pretty page.

items.question: Who brings the buyers after launch?
items.answer: We hand the site over ready for advertising: analytics connected, goals configured, every enquiry traceable to its source. The advertising and visibility work itself we run together with our partners, prepared in parallel with the build so the site doesn't open into an empty room. The ad budget and the partners' work are billed separately from development — they are not part of the site price. Nobody guarantees search positions — not us, not our partners: you can guarantee the work, not a place in Google's auction.

faq.title: Questions about building an online store

items.question: How much does an online store cost?
items.answer: An online store built to launch starts from $1000. The exact cost depends on the number of integrations (1C, CRM, delivery) and catalog size. The estimate is free, within 24 hours.

items.question: How long does it take to build a store?
items.answer: An online store with integrations takes from 4 weeks. Exact timelines are fixed in the contract after the brief.

items.question: Can 1C be connected during development instead of afterward?
items.answer: Yes — two-way sync with 1C (stock, prices, orders) is part of the store build, not a separate add-on later.

items.question: What's the difference between a store and a landing page with a cart?
items.answer: A landing page is a single page with an order form, from $350. An online store is a full catalog, cart, payment, delivery and accounting integrations, from $1000.

items.question: What's included in the store price?
items.answer: The site, catalog, cart, payment, and baseline delivery integrations. The contract fixes the timeline and budget; the warranty covers 12 months after handover.

items.question: This is my first move online. What do you need from me?
items.answer: A product list — a supplier's Excel price list is fine. Photos, if you have them. The details needed to accept payments — we'll tell you which ones. We fill the catalogue: the price list becomes product pages with specs and copy. Payments, delivery and fiscal receipts we connect ourselves.

items.question: Do I need a registered business and a till to sell online?
items.answer: Accepting payments on a website requires a registered business and fiscalisation — the exact form is best agreed with your accountant, we don't advise on tax. On our side: we'll tell you which details are needed to connect payments, and configure the till so that an order creates the receipt and the waybill by itself.

items.question: Is there actually demand — is it too late to open a store now?
items.answer: In 2025 Ukrainians spent ₴256bn on online purchases — 196m orders at an average basket of about ₴1,320 (WayForPay data). Online sellers' revenue in dollar terms grew 36% in H2 2025 even as order counts fell (Promodo study). These are industry figures, not a promise about your result: that depends on the niche, the product and the advertising. What's realistic in your niche we'll work out on the free assessment.
